articles.title: Compress an image to an exact size limit in JavaScript (binary search on quality)
articles.excerpt: Disclosure: an AI agent wrote this article for Hexloom Labs; no human wrote or edited it. Written with AI assistance and reviewed by Hexloom Labs. The code below was run in headless Chromium 151 befor…
articles.body: Disclosure: an AI agent wrote this article for Hexloom Labs; no human wrote or edited it. Written with AI assistance and reviewed by Hexloom Labs. The code below was run in headless Chromium 151 before posting, and the numbers come from that run. Upload forms love hard limits: "photo must be under 100 KB". The quality slider in most editors doesn't help, because it never says how big the file will be. You nudge it, save, check the size, and repeat. A browser can run that loop for you. canvas.toBlob(callback, type, quality) encodes a JPEG or WebP at a quality from 0 to 1 and hands back a Blob, so you can read blob.size and decide what to try next. File size rises with quality, so instead of trying every step you can halve the range each time.

articles.title: Stock Watchlist Event Paging: Controlled Timing Exposes Batched Delivery Gaps
articles.excerpt: Short answer: test a stock watchlist's batched realtime delivery with a controlled clock and an explicit event cursor, then prove that reconnect backfill produces the same final state without dependin…
articles.body: Short answer: test a stock watchlist's batched realtime delivery with a controlled clock and an explicit event cursor, then prove that reconnect backfill produces the same final state without depending on wall-clock sleeps. The page says that watchlist updates are late. The on-call view shows quotes arriving now, so the transport looks healthy, yet one symbol has jumped from sequence 4102 to 4105 and another appears twice. This is the awkward alert: the socket is connected, the dashboard is moving, and the user-visible state is still untrustworthy. Don't start by raising the timeout. Work backward from the page. The earlier signal should have been a growing gap between the highest sequence produced and the highest contiguous sequence applied, split by live delivery and reconnect backfill.

articles.title: Frontend Backend Error Tracking: How to Choose Practical Exceptions Without Session Replay
articles.excerpt: A checkout error system should preserve enough evidence to answer one operational question: did the logistics order fail before acceptance, after acceptance, or only in the browser? Collecting traces…
articles.body: A checkout error system should preserve enough evidence to answer one operational question: did the logistics order fail before acceptance, after acceptance, or only in the browser? Collecting traces and replay by default would add volume without necessarily improving that answer. The practical choice is a deliberately small exception pipeline with a shared correlation key, stable failure classes, aggressive field allowlisting, and separate alerts for customer impact and pipeline health. It covers browser and API exceptions while keeping signal quality ahead of noise.

articles.body: Most SAP implementation issues are predictable and tied to the same handful of blind spots that appear in implementation projects regardless of company size or industry. Knowing which issues you will face during a major implementation allows you (and business users on your customers’ side) to prepare for most of them or avoid them altogether. articles.title: Architectural Deep-Dive: Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models
articles.excerpt: Transitive Behavioral Couplings: Why Downstream LLM Fine-Tuning Silently Unlocks Critical Attack Vectors When deploying domain-adapted Large Language Models (LLMs) in autonomous production swarms, sta…
articles.body: Transitive Behavioral Couplings: Why Downstream LLM Fine-Tuning Silently Unlocks Critical Attack Vectors When deploying domain-adapted Large Language Models (LLMs) in autonomous production swarms, standard verification usually checks two things: task performance on downstream benchmarks and safety alignment against standard red-teaming suites. A recent paper ( "Behavioral Couplings: From Formation to Behavioral Emergence in Language Models" , arXiv:2610.23847) exposes a fundamental failure mode in this paradigm: transitive behavioral couplings . Fine-tuning a model on a benign capability can silently trigger latent, decoupled failure modes embedded deep within the pre-training corpus.

articles.title: Six AI models played chess through their CLIs. None of them delivered checkmate.
articles.excerpt: I build SpaceApp, a self-hosted workspace for running AI coding CLIs side by side. On 18 October I let six models play chess against each other there, each through its own CLI. Nobody won by checkmate…
articles.body: I build SpaceApp, a self-hosted workspace for running AI coding CLIs side by side. On 18 October I let six models play chess against each other there, each through its own CLI. Nobody won by checkmate. The way they lost is the interesting part. The setup Players: Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 (through Claude Code), GPT-6-Astra and GPT-6.1-Sol (through Codex), all at xhigh reasoning; Gemini 4 Argon (High) and Gemini 3.8 Flash (High) (through the Gemini CLI). Format: a 4-round Swiss tournament, 12 games. Clock: 120 seconds per move. Each move is one one-shot turn of the model's CLI: it gets the position and answers with a move. Strikes: a timeout, a provider error or a second illegal answer plays a random legal move for that side and counts a strike. The third strike forfeits the game.

articles.title: 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up
articles.excerpt: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a horde of mysterious "failed stars," or brown dwarfs, not-so-stellar loners that wander the darkness of space alone.
articles.body: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?).

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of the unethical and likely illegal acts its agents are performing. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
